AlberdiLab | hilldiv3 manuscript Microflora Danica worked example: staged data Alberdi Lab Last update: 2026-10-07 Chapter 1 Introduction This webbook contains the data and reproducible code for the Microflora Danica worked example in the hilldiv3 manuscript. The staged release contains sample and genome metadata, a representative MAG abundance matrix, and a phylogenetic tree. Analysis chapters will be added as the remaining work is run. 1.1 Prepare the R environment 1.1.1 Environment Clone the GitHub repository and open hilldiv3-ms.Rproj, or create a new RStudio project from: https://github.com/alberdilab/hilldiv3-ms.git 1.1.2 Libraries The current data preparation chapter uses these R packages: library(data.table) library(ape) library(knitr) 1.2 Analysis steps 1.2.1 Step 0 - Data preparation The data preparation chapter describes the committed Microflora Danica panel, loads it, and checks its sample, genome, abundance, and tree alignment. The source-download and preparation scripts are in scripts/. Functional annotations and hilldiv3 analyses will follow in later chapters.

Chapter 2 Data preparation The staged panel contains 360 geographically dispersed Microflora Danica samples: 45 from each of eight habitat classes. It uses the same locked sample and representative genome selections as the gifter case study. 2.1 Input data File Contents data/mag_relative_abundance.tsv.xz Relative abundances for 5,518 representative MAGs (rows) and 360 samples (columns). The first column is genome_id. data/sample_metadata.tsv Sample metadata in abundance-column order, including habitat class, ontology, location, date, and selection audit. data/representative_metadata.tsv Metadata for the 95% ANI species representatives in abundance-row order. data/representative_tree.nwk Source tree pruned to the 5,518 representative genome_id tips, retaining source branch lengths. 2.2 Load the staged panel The committed tables and tree are the input to the forthcoming analyses. Load them from the repository root: sample_metadata <- data.table::fread( "data/sample_metadata.tsv", data.table = FALSE ) genome_metadata <- data.table::fread( "data/representative_metadata.tsv", data.table = FALSE ) genome_abundance <- data.table::fread( cmd = "xz -dc data/mag_relative_abundance.tsv.xz", data.table = FALSE, check.names = FALSE ) genome_tree <- ape::read.tree("data/representative_tree.nwk") The selected panel has 45 samples in each habitat class: habitats <- table(sample_metadata$habitat_label) knitr::kable( data.frame(habitat = names(habitats), samples = as.integer(habitats)), col.names = c("Habitat", "Samples") ) Habitat Samples Agricultural field soil 45 Natural bog/fen soil 45 Natural forest soil 45 Natural freshwater sediment 45 Natural grassland soil 45 Natural saltwater sediment 45 Urban greenspace soil 45 Urban wastewater water 45 2.3 Check the staged objects The abundance rows and columns must align with the metadata, and the tree must contain exactly the representative genomes: stopifnot( nrow(sample_metadata) == 360L, nrow(genome_metadata) == 5518L, nrow(genome_abundance) == 5518L, ncol(genome_abundance) == 361L, length(habitats) == 8L, all(habitats == 45L), identical(genome_abundance$genome_id, genome_metadata$genome_id), identical(names(genome_abundance)[-1L], sample_metadata$sample_id), setequal(genome_tree$tip.label, genome_metadata$genome_id) ) profile_totals <- colSums(as.matrix(genome_abundance[-1L])) stopifnot(all(is.finite(profile_totals)), all(profile_totals > 0.99 & profile_totals < 1.01)) cat(sprintf( "%d samples, %d representative genomes, %d tree tips; profile sums %.6f–%.6f.\n", nrow(sample_metadata), nrow(genome_metadata), ape::Ntip(genome_tree), min(profile_totals), max(profile_totals) )) 360 samples, 5518 representative genomes, 5518 tree tips; profile sums 0.999988–1.000015. The abundance values are proportions of the published MFD MAG profile, not genome or read counts. The preparation script keeps strain (t__) rows from the Sylph profiles, maps MAGs to their published secondary_cluster, sums each 95% ANI cluster, and divides percentages by 100. It assigns each cluster profile to the deposited representative MAG. It does not renormalize profiles. The representative abundance therefore stands for its cluster; it does not imply that all members have identical gene content. These values describe the MFD MAG profile, not the fraction of all DNA in each sample. 2.4 Sources The primary study is Singleton and colleagues, The Microflora Danica atlas of Danish environmental microbiomes. The Microflora Danica data deposit provides Nitrifiers.tar.gz, including the published MAG metadata and Sylph abundance table. Please cite both the study and deposit when using these data, and consult the deposit for its reuse terms. The sample and representative tables are copies of the locked panels at gifter commit f04f7de. The source tree is gtdb-shallow.tree from the MFD companion repository at commit 957591d. Tips outside the representative panel were removed. 2.5 Rebuild and verify The committed files are ready to use. To rebuild them from the pinned public sources, install R packages data.table and ape, then run: bash scripts/fetch-source-data.sh Rscript scripts/prepare-data.R Rscript scripts/check-data.R The source archive is about 228 MB. Downloads remain in the ignored sources/ directory. The preparation script also accepts paths to existing MAG metadata, abundance TSV.xz, and source tree files, in that order. To verify the committed snapshot byte for byte: shasum -a 256 -c data/SHA256SUMS The checker verifies sample and genome IDs, 45 samples per habitat, table ordering, finite nonnegative abundances, near-unit profile sums, and exact tree-tip identity. In this snapshot, sample profile totals range from 0.999988 to 1.000015.
